lessons.title: Recognize Common Power Tools
lessons.objective: Match common power tool categories to jobs.
lessons.why_this_matters: Customers may ask for a tool by its appearance instead of the task it performs.

content_sections.heading: Drilling and driving
paragraphs: Drills create holes with suitable bits. Drivers install or remove compatible fasteners. Impact drivers are a distinct category with different operating characteristics.

content_sections.heading: Cutting and shaping
paragraphs: Circular saws and jigsaws cut suitable materials with the correct blade. Sanders remove or smooth surface material. Grinders have different hazards and uses.

content_sections.heading: Power sources
paragraphs: Corded tools use mains electricity. Cordless tools use compatible battery systems. Do not assume batteries, chargers, or accessories are interchangeable.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer wants a tool to assemble furniture. You ask what fasteners are included and whether the instructions recommend a hand tool or powered driver.
what_to_say_or_do: Ask what task the tool must perform.
common_mistakes: Assuming all batteries fit all tools.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Refer tool-specific operation and hazardous applications to manufacturer instructions or a qualified specialist.

supporting_materials.purpose: Identify tool/fastener features and compare real products
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Drills create holes with suitable bits.
Ask what task the tool must perform.
Refer tool-specific operation and hazardous applications to manufacturer instructions or a qualified specialist.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer wants a tool to assemble furniture. You ask what fasteners are included and whether the instructions recommend a hand tool or powered driver.
unscored_practice.answer: Ask what task the tool must perform. Identify the material.
unscored_practice.explanation: Customers may ask for a tool by its appearance instead of the task it performs. Refer tool-specific operation and hazardous applications to manufacturer instructions or a qualified specialist.

lessons.title: Compare Corded and Cordless Options
lessons.objective: Explain practical differences without unsupported claims.
lessons.why_this_matters: The best power source depends on the work area and the tool requirements.

content_sections.heading: Corded tools
paragraphs: Corded tools need an appropriate electrical supply and may suit work where a suitable outlet is available. Cord management is part of safe use.

content_sections.heading: Cordless tools
paragraphs: Cordless tools use a battery and charger approved for the tool. Runtime varies by task, battery, and tool. Do not promise a fixed runtime without verified data.

content_sections.heading: Ask useful questions
paragraphs: Where will the tool be used? Is power available? How often will it be used? Does the customer already own a compatible battery platform?

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer needs a drill for projects around a large property. You ask whether outlets are nearby and whether they already own batteries in a particular tool system.
common_mistakes: Assuming higher voltage always means the better tool.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask for help with electrical supply, battery compatibility, or tool selection for hazardous environments.

supporting_materials.purpose: Identify tool/fastener features and compare real products
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Corded tools need an appropriate electrical supply and may suit work where a suitable outlet is available.
Ask for help with electrical supply, battery compatibility, or tool selection for hazardous environments.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer needs a drill for projects around a large property. You ask whether outlets are nearby and whether they already own batteries in a particular tool system.
unscored_practice.answer: Ask about access to power. Check existing battery systems.
unscored_practice.explanation: The best power source depends on the work area and the tool requirements. Ask for help with electrical supply, battery compatibility, or tool selection for hazardous environments.

lessons.title: Understand Bits, Blades, and Accessories
lessons.objective: Recognize that accessories must match the tool and material.
lessons.why_this_matters: An incorrect accessory can damage a project or create serious injury risk.

content_sections.heading: Match the connection
paragraphs: Drill bits, saw blades, and other accessories use specific shanks, mounts, or arbor sizes. Check the tool and accessory documentation.

content_sections.heading: Match the material
paragraphs: A blade or bit suitable for wood may not be suitable for masonry or metal. Verify intended materials and limitations on packaging.

content_sections.heading: Check operating limits
paragraphs: Accessories may have speed or other ratings. Never recommend an accessory that exceeds or conflicts with tool instructions. Guards and safety devices must remain in place.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer brings a photo of a circular saw and asks for a blade. You ask for the exact model and check the blade diameter, arbor, material, and tool instructions.
what_to_say_or_do: Verify intended material and operating limits.
common_mistakes: Choosing a blade by diameter alone.
Suggesting removal of a guard to fit an accessory.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Escalate all unclear accessory fit, speed ratings, and guard questions to manufacturer documentation or a qualified specialist.

supporting_materials.purpose: Identify tool/fastener features and compare real products
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Drill bits, saw blades, and other accessories use specific shanks, mounts, or arbor sizes.
Escalate all unclear accessory fit, speed ratings, and guard questions to manufacturer documentation or a qualified specialist.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer brings a photo of a circular saw and asks for a blade. You ask for the exact model and check the blade diameter, arbor, material, and tool instructions.
unscored_practice.answer: Find the exact tool model. Check mounting dimensions.
unscored_practice.explanation: An incorrect accessory can damage a project or create serious injury risk. Escalate all unclear accessory fit, speed ratings, and guard questions to manufacturer documentation or a qualified specialist.

lessons.title: Teach Safety Before Features
lessons.objective: Explain basic power tool safety and limits of retail advice.
lessons.why_this_matters: Power tools can cause serious injuries. Sales advice must not replace training or instructions.

content_sections.heading: Read instructions first
paragraphs: Manufacturer manuals explain guards, personal protective equipment, setup, and operation. Never tell customers to bypass safeguards.

content_sections.heading: Prevent accidental starts
paragraphs: Tools must be handled according to manufacturer guidance when changing accessories, transporting, or storing them. Unplugging or removing the battery may be required depending on the tool and task.

content_sections.heading: Recognize high-risk jobs
paragraphs: Electrical, structural, overhead, and unfamiliar cutting tasks may require qualified help. Retail associates should not provide unverified operating or installation instructions.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks whether they can remove a saw guard for a difficult cut. You explain that safety devices should not be bypassed and refer to the tool manual and a qualified professional.
what_to_say_or_do: Discuss required protective equipment as specified.
common_mistakes: Demonstrating an unfamiliar tool without authorization.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a supervisor before any in-store demonstration; refer complex or high-risk operation to trained professionals.

supporting_materials.purpose: Illustrate the correct selection or safe tool-handling decision
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Manufacturer manuals explain guards, personal protective equipment, setup, and operation.
Ask a supervisor before any in-store demonstration; refer complex or high-risk operation to trained professionals.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer asks whether they can remove a saw guard for a difficult cut. You explain that safety devices should not be bypassed and refer to the tool manual and a qualified professional.
unscored_practice.answer: Point customers to the manual. Discuss required protective equipment as specified.
unscored_practice.explanation: Power tools can cause serious injuries. Sales advice must not replace training or instructions. Ask a supervisor before any in-store demonstration; refer complex or high-risk operation to trained professionals.

lessons.title: Help Customers Choose and Maintain Tools
lessons.objective: Guide a responsible purchase and service handoff.
lessons.why_this_matters: A complete recommendation includes the tool, compatible accessories, and realistic care needs.

content_sections.heading: Match the project and frequency
paragraphs: Ask what tasks the customer will do and how often. Compare manufacturer-listed capacity and included items.

content_sections.heading: Check the box
paragraphs: Some tools are sold without batteries or chargers. Verify package contents and compatible accessories before checkout.

content_sections.heading: Support care and service
paragraphs: Explain that cleaning, storage, inspection, and maintenance follow the owner’s manual. Do not invent warranty coverage or service promises.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer selects a cordless drill kit. You check whether the box includes a battery, charger, and bits. You explain where to find the owner’s manual and store service information if applicable.
what_to_say_or_do: Refer maintenance and warranty questions to verified documentation.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Refer uncertain repairs, service eligibility, and warranty coverage to the store manager or manufacturer.

supporting_materials.purpose: Illustrate the correct selection or safe tool-handling decision
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Ask what tasks the customer will do and how often.
Refer uncertain repairs, service eligibility, and warranty coverage to the store manager or manufacturer.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer selects a cordless drill kit. You check whether the box includes a battery, charger, and bits. You explain where to find the owner’s manual and store service information if applicable.
unscored_practice.answer: Ask about intended jobs. Verify box contents.
unscored_practice.explanation: A complete recommendation includes the tool, compatible accessories, and realistic care needs. Refer uncertain repairs, service eligibility, and warranty coverage to the store manager or manufacturer.
